elements.quote: Previous studies have examined the diagnostic and prognostic performance of the aforementioned scoring systems in sepsis patients. The proportion of DIC in sepsis when applying ISTH-DIC criteria ranged from 16% to 45% [18, 19], while the proportion based on JAAM-- DIC criteria ranged from 29% to 91% [20, 21]. Based on the SIC criteria, the proportion of coagulopathy in sepsis patients ranged from 22% to 86% [19, 22]. Similar variability in mortality rate and predictive performance of outcomes have been observed.
elements.reason: The introduction describes the current state of knowledge, reporting ranges of prevalence and variability in diagnostic/prognostic performance and mechanisms, indicating important uncertainties.

elements.quote: However, pooled estimate of the proportion of positive scores, mortality rate, and predictive performance of these scores, by making use of meta-analysis in sepsis patients is lacking. This systematic review and metaanalysis assessed the proportion of DIC and coagulopathy in sepsis patients based on the ISTH-DIC, JAAM-DIC, and SIC criteria and evaluated their performance in predicting mortality in sepsis patients.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states a gap (lack of pooled estimates) and explains the need and purpose of the current review to fill that gap.
No evidence was found that discusses existing similar systematic reviews, the need for the current review in relation to them, or citation of prior reviews.

elements.quote: This study aimed to determine the score positivity rate and performance of different DIC scoring systems in predicting mortality in sepsis patients.
elements.reason: The review addresses diagnostic/prognostic scoring systems, not intervention effects; therefore a mechanism of action for an intervention is not applicable.

elements.quote: This study aimed to determine the score positivity rate and performance of different DIC scoring systems in predicting mortality in sepsis patients.
elements.reason: The review evaluates diagnostic scoring systems rather than complex interventions or delivery contexts, so a logic model is not applicable.

elements.quote: Studies were included based on the following inclusion criteria: 1) studies involved sepsis patients; (2) observational studies; 3) studies that describe data about DIC diagnosis based on any of the three criteria (ISTH-DIC, JAAM-DIC, and SIC); 4) studies that reported the relationship between DIC diagnosis and at least one of the following outcomes: sensitivity or specificity or AUC to predict mortality. Studies were excluded if they were conference abstracts, case studies, reports of the same study, reviews, studies which did not report sensitivity, specificity, or data to calculate the score performance characteristics.
elements.reason: The chunk explicitly lists the study characteristics used for eligibility: population (sepsis patients), study design (observational), index tests (DIC diagnosis by ISTH/JAAM/SIC), and required outcomes (sensitivity/specificity/AUC). It also lists exclusions such as conference abstracts and duplicate reports.

elements.quote: Studies were excluded if they were conference abstracts, case studies, reports of the same study, reviews, studies which did not report sensitivity, specificity, or data to calculate the score performance characteristics.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies some report-type restrictions (e.g., excluding conference abstracts, reviews, duplicate reports) but does not state any restrictions or eligibility criteria related to dissemination year or language, so report-characteristic eligibility is only partially specified.

elements.reason: The PRISMA flow figure (chunk text_15) lists 'Wrong outcomes (n = 26)' as a reason for exclusion (indicating outcomes not measured or irrelevant), and chunk text_10 separately states exclusion of studies that 'did not report sensitivity, specificity, or data to calculate' (indicating exclusion for not reporting outcome results), demonstrating the review distinguishes the two types of exclusion.

elements.quote: Seven studies compared the performance of ISTH and JAAM score, four studies compared ISTH and SIC, two studies compared JAAM and SIC, and three studies compared all the three scores.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the groups used in syntheses and links them to the comparisons of interest (pairwise and three-way comparisons among ISTH, JAAM, and SIC), indicating how studies were grouped for synthesis.

elements.quote: In total, 5557 studies were initially identified from four databases (1882 studies from Embase, 1753 studies from Scopus, 1080 studies from Web of science, and 842 studies from Medline). After removing 2553 duplicates, 3004 studies were eligible for screening. Out of these studies, 2914 were excluded based on title and abstract screening. A total of 90 studies underwent fulltext review, out of which 69 studies were excluded for the reasons indicated in Fig 1. Finally, a total of 21 studies were eligible for the systematic review and meta-analysis.

elements.quote: Twenty-one studies, published between 2009 and 2024, comprising 9319 sepsis patients were included.
